quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the car ahead.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian who might move into your lane. If a driver in the next lane is tailgating, they may try to pass and cut in front of you. If you see someone in a parked car or a pedestrian in the street, use your horn as you pass. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders together for a better view.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must finish passing without going over the speed limit.
You may finish a pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must finish passing without going over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed at or below the speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
Stopping sooner than you expect.
Getting a flat tire.
Taking longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause your wheels to lose grip and skid, which can result in a crash.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?

options.text: With your right hand
With your left hand
With your right foot
With your left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With your right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and you control it with your right hand.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them well or put them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads high on the seat or frame because this raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and throws off the balance. Spread loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to look over your shoulder if you check your mirrors.
Your mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
You can trust that other drivers will respond to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than a walking pace, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction of your turn causes the motorcycle to lean correctly.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: You are riding in heavy traffic.
You are riding during the day in good conditions.
There are two lanes in each direction.
You do not expect stopping to take longer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are riding in heavy traffic.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are not ideal. You should do this if the road is slippery, if you cannot see past the car ahead, if you are riding at night, or if traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
Riding conditions are normal.
The road is wet.
You can see clearly past the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more space to stop than normal. Also increase it in heavy traffic or if you cannot see past the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your whole face.
It works less well than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your eyes and your face.
Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your face.
Neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield can protect your whole face during a crash.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to stay safer?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothes.
Wear bright-colored clothes.
Do not ride during the day.
Choose safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: To reduce your crash risk, make yourself visible by wearing bright-colored clothes when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Why should you check your mirrors when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To see if parked cars are entering traffic.
To see if other vehicles are changing lanes.
To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
To see if someone plans to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors at an intersection to see if cars are coming up behind you too fast. Drivers may not see you in time to stop.

questions.question: How should you secure a load in a sidecar?

options.text: Let the load move freely.
Secure it so the weight does not shift.
Place it loose in the seat.
Secure it near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it so the weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not move and affect handling. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handgrip.
On the right handgrip.
By the left foot peg.
By the right foot peg.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip.
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all controls before you start riding.

questions.question: What should passengers do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Lean when the operator leans.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean with them. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding the operator, holding onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning sign.
Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When are motorcyclists safest?

options.text: When they are seen by other drivers.
When they are faster than other vehicles.
When they are on the side of the road.
When they are on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are safest when other drivers can clearly see them. Use your headlight, brake light, signals, and lane position to be more visible.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park a motorcycle at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Does not mean they will yield to you when they should.
Guarantees that they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not notice them.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Go slower than usual.
Follow other vehicles more closely than when riding alone.
Go faster than usual.
Brake later than when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start braking earlier, increase your following distance, and leave larger gaps when crossing or entering traffic.

questions.question: To see better when riding at night, you can:

options.text: Use the headlights of the car in front of you.
Use your brake light.
Travel faster.
Follow other vehicles more closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see better by using the headlights of the vehicle ahead to light up the road. Increase your following distance and reduce your speed in the dark.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. If you must brake, gradually apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should ride:

options.text: In a single-file line.
In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Groups should normally ride in a staggered formation. However, switch to a single-file line when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
Always ride on the left side of your lane.
Not worry about your position in the lane.
Always ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. This position is most likely to show up in the rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, ride:

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In any part of your lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. Be ready to adjust your position as conditions change.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than daytime riding because you can see other vehicles' lights better.
Harder than daytime riding because visibility is worse.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than daytime riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than daytime riding because visibility is worse.
questions.explanation: Night riding is more difficult because you cannot see as well and it is harder for others to see you. Lack of natural light and shadows makes it harder to judge distances.

questions.question: Wobbling or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure.
Brakes that do not work properly.
A balanced load.
Strong wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with the right foot.
